title: Carignan
description: Also called Cariñena, Mazuelo, Samsó and Carignano. Once a bulk grape, now prized from old vines.
L: High acid, high tannin, old vines

Carignan gives deep-coloured wines with red and black fruit, dried herbs, liquorice and earthy, sometimes meaty notes. It has high acidity, high tannin and can be rustic and astringent when young or overcropped. From old, low-yielding vines, it becomes concentrated and complex.
Dark fruit, herbs, high acid and tannin

Carignan comes from Aragón, in Spain, near the town of Cariñena. In Spain it's also called Mazuelo, in Rioja, and Samsó, in Catalonia. In Italy, mainly Sardinia, it's Carignano. It buds late and ripens very late, so it needs heat. It's vigorous and can yield heavily, which is why it became a bulk grape.
Match each name to where it's used.
Carignan takes a new name in each region.

Carignan often appears in blends, adding colour, acidity and structure. On its own, look for deep colour, bright acidity, firm tannin and earthy, herbal notes. Old-vine examples are richer, with dark fruit and spice. Its high acidity sets it apart from Grenache, its usual partner.

Carignan was once France's most planted grape, especially in the Languedoc, where it made cheap, high-yield table wine. EU vine-pull schemes from the 1980s cut plantings dramatically. In Spain it grows in Priorat, Montsant, Empordà and Rioja. In Italy, Sardinia's Carignano del Sulcis is its stronghold.

In the Languedoc and Roussillon, Carignan blends with Grenache, Syrah and Mourvèdre, adding acidity and colour. In Priorat, it partners Garnacha. In Rioja, as Mazuelo, it's a minor partner to Tempranillo, adding acidity and colour. Carbonic maceration, the Beaujolais method, is sometimes used to soften it.
Why were many Languedoc Carignan vineyards pulled out from the 1980s?
EU schemes to reduce wine surplus
Vine-pull schemes targeted high-yield, low-value vineyards, many planted with Carignan.
Look for Vieilles Vignes, old vines, on Languedoc Carignan labels. Old-vine Carignan is far more concentrated than the bulk wine that gave it a poor reputation.
Which grapes does Carignan often blend with?
Riesling isn't a Mediterranean blending partner.
Carignan was France's most planted grape; plantings fell sharply
It blends with Grenache, Syrah and Mourvèdre
Old vines from Priorat to Maule

In Priorat, Carignan, called Cariñena or Samsó, grows on steep slopes of llicorella, dark slate. Old vines, many over 80 years, give tiny yields and concentrated, mineral wines. When producers revived Priorat in the late 1980s, old Cariñena with Garnacha was their raw material.

In Chile's Maule Valley, old, dry-farmed Carignan vines, some planted after the 1939 Chillán earthquake, were rediscovered. In 2009, producers founded VIGNO, Vignadores de Carignan, requiring at least 65% Carignan from dry-farmed vines over 30 years old, and two years' ageing. It became one of Chile's most exciting wines.
At least 65% Carignan from dry-farmed vines over 30 years old
VIGNO is a growers' association protecting old, dry-farmed Maule Carignan.

Old vines have deep roots that find water in dry soils, so they cope with drought without irrigation. Their naturally low yields concentrate the fruit, balancing Carignan's acidity and tannin. Young, high-yield Carignan is harsh and thin; old-vine Carignan is rich and complex.
Match each term to Carignan's revival.
Old vines turned Carignan's reputation around.
Priorat's old Cariñena on llicorella makes concentrated wines
Maule's VIGNO protects old, dry-farmed Carignan
Old vines balance Carignan's acidity and tannin

Carignan's acidity and tannin suit hearty Mediterranean food: cassoulet, grilled lamb, sausages, stews with olives and herbs, and roast vegetables. Its earthy, herbal notes match rosemary, thyme and garlic. Old-vine examples suit game and aged cheeses.
Serve at 16 to 18 degrees. Simple Carignan is best young. Old-vine wines from Priorat, Maule or the Languedoc can age 10 to 15 years, as acidity keeps them fresh. Decant young, firm examples.
Which dish suits an old-vine Carignan?
Hearty, fatty dishes balance its acidity and tannin.
Carbonic maceration Carignan, light and juicy, is a good chilled red for summer barbecues.
Carignan's high acidity helps old-vine examples age.
Yes. Acidity preserves freshness over time.
